topic.name: The Characteristic Properties of Acids & Bases

parts.problem_md:
Fig. 4.1 shows the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride using inert electrodes.

![Diagram of electrolysis: two electrodes in concentrated aqueous sodium chloride linked to a low-voltage d.c. supply, labelled positive and negative.](assets/001-diagram-of-electrolysis-two-electrodes-in-concen.png)

State the name of the positive electrode.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - The positive electrode is called the anode **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> A quick way to remember which electrode is which: the anode is the positive electrode, while the cathode is negative.

parts.problem_md:
Identify the gases produced at the electrodes.

positive electrode: ..................

negative electrode: ..................
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Positive electrode: chlorine, C*l*<sub>2</sub> **[1 mark]**
> - Negative electrode: hydrogen, H<sub>2</sub> **[1 mark]**
> 
> Ignore chloride

> **[exam-tip]**
> Don't confuse the chlorine gas (C*l*<sub>2</sub>) produced at the anode with chloride ions (C*l*<sup>-</sup>) still in solution — only the gas product should be named here.

parts.problem_md:
The electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride produces a solution containing an alkali.

(i) State what is meant by an alkali.

[1]

(ii) State what colour change is observed when methyl orange is added to a solution containing an alkali.

from orange to ...........................................................

[1]
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - (i) An alkali is a soluble base or metal oxide/hydroxide **[1 mark]**
> - (ii) Methyl orange turns yellow in an alkali **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Remember methyl orange is red in an acid and yellow in an alkali — the colour change described here is specifically "from orange to yellow".

parts.problem_md:
The electrolysis shown in Fig. 4.1 produces the alkali sodium hydroxide.

Aqueous sodium hydroxide reacts with dilute sulfuric acid.

(i) Complete the word equation for this reaction.

![Diagram of a word equation: sodium hydroxide plus sulfuric acid arrow blank box plus blank box, for students to fill in the reaction products.](assets/002-diagram-of-a-word-equation-sodium-hydroxide-plus.png)

[1]

(ii) The reaction between aqueous sodium hydroxide and dilute sulfuric acid is exothermic.

State what is meant by an exothermic reaction.

[2]
parts.solution_md:
(i)

![Text equation showing sodium hydroxide plus sulfuric acid arrow producing sodium sulfate and water, illustrating a neutralisation reaction](assets/003-text-equation-showing-sodium-hydroxide-plus-sulf.png)

**[1 mark]**

(ii)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - An exothermic reaction transfers thermal energy to the surroundings **[1 mark]**
> - This leads to an increase in temperature of the surroundings **[1 mark]**
> 
> Idea of the surroundings may be seen in either marking point

> **[exam-tip]**
> A common mistake is describing energy changes only in terms of the reacting chemicals — always mention the surroundings when defining exothermic or endothermic reactions.

parts.problem_md:
Which row identifies the formulas of an acidic oxide and a basic oxide?

|   | acidic oxide | basic oxide |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | NO<sub>2</sub> | CaO |
| **B** | SO<sub>2</sub> | CO<sub>2</sub> |
| **C** | CuO | Na<sub>2</sub>O |
| **D** | Li<sub>2</sub>O | SiO<sub>2</sub> |
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- Acidic oxides are formed when a non-metal element combines with oxygen; NO<sub>2</sub> is an example of an acidic oxide
- Basic oxides are formed when a metal element combines with oxygen; CaO is an example of a basic oxide

**B** is incorrect because CO<sub>2</sub> is also an acidic oxide, not a basic oxide

**C** is incorrect because both CuO and Na<sub>2</sub>O are basic oxides

**D** is incorrect because Li<sub>2</sub>O is a basic oxide and SiO<sub>2</sub> is an acidic oxide, so the columns are reversed

parts.problem_md:
The products of a reaction are water, calcium chloride and carbon dioxide only.

Which reaction mixture gives these products?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- The reaction between a metal carbonate and an acid produces a salt, water and carbon dioxide
- Calcium carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid to produce calcium chloride, water and carbon dioxide

CaCO<sub>3</sub> + 2HCl → CaCl<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O + CO<sub>2</sub>

**A** is incorrect because calcium reacting with an acid produces a salt and hydrogen only, not water or carbon dioxide

**B** is incorrect because calcium hydroxide reacting with an acid produces a salt and water only, not carbon dioxide

**D** is incorrect because calcium oxide reacting with an acid produces a salt and water only, not carbon dioxide
